A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–G. Text comparison and visual inspection support matching the methods, proofs, experiments, tables, and figures despite pagination shifts.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on manipulated and naturally trained SE-GNNs, faithfulness-metric evaluations, and supplementary analyses, with numerical outcomes in Tables 2–4, 6, and 8–10.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including the CPatchMNIST study, perturbation-budget analysis, and supplementary explanation case studies.

M1.justification: The attack objective in Eq. (3), EST definition in Eq. (5), sampling procedure in Algorithm 1, and SE-GNN implementation components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate RBGV, MNISTsp, MUTAG, SST2P, and CPatchMNIST under the same malicious-training, natural-training, and supplementary test scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated SE-GNNs remain GSAT, DIR, and SMGNN. Corresponding metric comparisons retain the same participants, including Fid-/+, RFid-/+, Suf, Nec, and CF in Table 3 and the same smaller comparator sets in subsequent experiments.

E3.justification: The training settings, data splits, explanation thresholds, evaluation metrics, and rejection criteria remain unchanged. Section 5.1 retains the 50-perturbation budget, and Appendix D retains the same experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same perturbation-budget ablation in Figure 2, attack-failure analysis in Appendix E.3, sufficiency sanity check in Appendix E.4, and natural-training case studies. None receives new or revised evidence.

E5.justification: Five-seed averaging for Table 2 and the existing standard-deviation reporting are unchanged. Appendix D.3 also retains the same stated SST2P exclusions of SMGNN seed 5 and DIR seed 3.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries and qualitative findings in the main text and appendices match. For example, Table 2 retains attacked GSAT's MNISTsp accuracy of 93.8 ± 0.1 and F1 score of 93.6 ± 0.4. Relocated tables contain no new results.

T1.justification: Appendix F.3 replaces 'Degenerate' with 'Non-label-preserving' in Definition 5 and Theorem 3, matching the terminology already used in the definition heading and proof. The condition f(G) ≠ f(R), mathematical arguments, assumptions, and other theoretical results are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about optimal-risk degenerate explanations, malicious and natural failures, weaknesses of existing faithfulness metrics, and EST's contribution.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including possible OOD-induced rejection by EST, its inability to detect redundancy-based unfaithfulness, and the attack's training-access assumption. The Appendix F.3 terminology correction introduces no new interpretation.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement replaces the supplemental-code pointer with an explicit GitHub repository link, while the abstract's supplemental-code sentence is removed. This changes documented code-access instructions; Appendix D's implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7, Appendix C, and the cited research works retain the same content and positioning. The adjusted citation grammar in Appendix D does not introduce a different source.

P1.justification: v3 adds a funding acknowledgement, corrects terminology in Definition 5 and Theorem 3, and makes small grammar, punctuation, and author-footnote edits. The scientific narrative and section organization remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: Author affiliations are compacted, text and footnotes reflow, and Table 9 moves from page 29 to page 30. The figures, table structures, captions, and displayed scientific content remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 makes Definition 5 and Theorem 3 consistent with their existing heading and proof, reducing terminology confusion, and provides clearer code-location information through an explicit repository link. These are limited improvements in clarity and reproducibility documentation; the scientific methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
